doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Starting on banjo, piano, clarinet and trombone before drums
summary: He tried several instruments, ended on drums because of braces, and says he would go back to trombone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well you started out — was drums your first instrument?

No. That’s what I wound up with. I started with banjo, then piano, clarinet, trombone, and I’d probably still be playing that if I didn’t have to have braces. And drums was something convenient to play that your teeth can be bound up and it doesn’t really matter. And I just stayed with drums. With a crystal ball, I’d go back to trombone.
A little bit easier to move around.
That doesn’t bother me at all. I just like the trombone and I have a way I’d like to hear it sound, and I don’t hear it that often and I wish I could do it.
Yeah. There’s not a lot of young trombone players out there right now it doesn’t seem like, that the instrument is that much in fashion.
Not in the traditional and swing mode. There are some fine modern players, or clinicians, but not fellows who play real old style.
